The '''2006–07 Scottish Premier League''' season was the ninth season of the [[Scottish Premier League]]. It began on 29 July 2006.

The [[Scottish football champions|league champions]], [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and [[Runner-up|runners-up]], [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League]] on the return of [[Walter Smith]] as manager following a brief and disastrous reign by [[France|Frenchman]] [[Paul Le Guen]]. The team finishing third, [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] qualified for the [[UEFA Cup]], as did the [[Scottish Cup]] finalists [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]. However, being the bottom-placed team in the SPL, Dunfermline were also relegated to the [[Scottish First Division|First Division]].

==Events==
{{Main|2006–07 in Scottish football}}

*On 22 April 2007 [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] beat [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] 2–1 to win the title for the second season running thanks to goals from [[Jan Vennegoor of Hesselink]] and [[Shunsuke Nakamura]] who scored a free-kick in the dying second of the match to clinch the title for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]
*On 12 May 2007 [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] were relegated to the First Division after a 2–1 defeat at [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness CT]] and [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] came back from 2–0 down to win 3–2 at [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].
*On 20 May 2007 [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] beat [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] 2–0 at home in their final game of the season to qualify for the UEFA Cup.
*For the second consecutive season, the top scorer was [[Kris Boyd]] of [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], with 20 goals.
